hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? do you remember a word a child in your life learned and said proudly?
options: those are the best. today, the first words of all.
a big day. today’s story is a big day too.
that’s okay. today, every word, from the start.

steps.line: Yesterday the angels asked why. Now God answers, not with an argument, but a test. He sets things before them: “Tell Me their names.”
The angels answer honestly: “Glory be to You. We know nothing except what You have taught us.”

steps.q: The angels can’t name them. What do you think God does next?
o: Tells the angels the names Himself
Has Adam name them for the angels
Teaches the angels and Adam together
steps.why: God doesn’t argue. He lets Adam show them, one name at a time.

steps.line: God had taught Adam all the names. “Adam, tell them,” He said. And Adam named them, one by one.
“Didn’t I tell you,” God said, “that I know the hidden things of the heavens and the earth?”

steps.q: Why might naming be the answer to the angels’ question?
o: This creature can be taught, thing by thing
Names give the power to command things
It proved Adam was more obedient
steps.why: Not strength, not goodness: being teachable. That’s what the angels hadn’t seen yet.

steps.pre: God had told the angels He would place on earth a khalifa: a
steps.why: Khalifa: one who stands in for another. Many translate it vicegerent or steward, someone who looks after the earth, not its owner. Knowing the names is part of the job.

steps.line: What were the names? The Qur’an doesn’t say. One early scholar said everything, down to a bowl and a cooking pot.
Today, a toddler points. Dog. Ball. Moon. Each word, a small victory. Once a child can say moon, they can ask where it goes in the day.
steps.label: today

steps.q: The Qur’an doesn’t say what the names were. Ibn Abbas said: everything, even a bowl and a pot. What’s he getting at?
o: Every ordinary thing is worth knowing
The angels already knew the grand things
steps.why: Ibn Abbas, the Prophet’s ﷺ cousin and a great early interpreter, said it. Big or small, everything was named, so everything can be noticed.

steps.line: And grown-ups keep learning names: a bird, a tree, a neighbor’s name you never asked. To name a thing is to notice it.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. the angels didn’t pretend. “we know only what you taught us.” no shame in that, only honesty.
in islam, knowledge is a gift from God, and being teachable is part of being human. the qur’an gives a short prayer for it: my Lord, increase me in knowledge.

steps.q: The angels didn’t know, and said so. In the Qur’an’s telling, what made their answer good, not shameful?
o: They promised to learn the names later
They knew more than they let on
They admitted it, and praised God
steps.why: “Glory be to You. We know only what You taught us.” Honest not-knowing, turned into praise, is where learning starts.

today.say: today, learn one name you’ve walked past: a tree on your street, a bird at the window, the name of the person who makes your coffee. if you like, add the qur’an’s short prayer: rabbi zidni ‘ilma, my Lord, increase me in knowledge.
options: lovely. to name is to notice.
beautiful. it’s three words in arabic.

tomorrow.line: every angel bows. all but one. and his reason sounds very familiar.

sources: Qur’an 2:31-33 (“And He taught Adam all the names… They said: Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us… He said: Did I not tell you that I know the secret of the heavens and the earth?” Pickthall)
al-Tabari, Tafsir on 2:31 (Ibn ‘Abbas: the names of everything, even the bowl and the cooking pot)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4476 (the hadith of intercession: “Allah taught you the names of all things”)
Qur’an 20:114 (“My Lord! Increase me in knowledge”)
